Let

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{m=1}^{100}2^{-\lfloor 101k/m\rfloor}.
\]

All terms are nonnegative, so we may interchange the order of summation.

For a fixed \(m\), write every positive integer \(k\) uniquely as

\[
k=qm+r,\qquad q\ge 0,\quad 1\le r\le m.
\]

Then

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{101k}{m}\right\rfloor
=\left\lfloor \frac{101(qm+r)}{m}\right\rfloor
=101q+\left\lfloor \frac{101r}{m}\right\rfloor.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}2^{-\lfloor 101k/m\rfloor}
=
\left(\sum_{q=0}^{\infty}2^{-101q}\right)
\left(\sum_{r=1}^{m}2^{-\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor}\right).
\]

Since

\[
\sum_{q=0}^{\infty}2^{-101q}=\frac{1}{1-2^{-101}},
\]

we get

\[
S=\frac{1}{1-2^{-101}}
\sum_{m=1}^{100}\sum_{r=1}^{m}2^{-\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor}.
\]

Now let

\[
B=\sum_{m=1}^{100}\sum_{r=1}^{m}2^{-\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor}.
\]

Fix \(m\). Since \(101\) is prime and \(1\le m\le 100\), we have \(\gcd(101,m)=1\).

- The value \(\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor=101\) occurs only at \(r=m\).
- The value \(100\) occurs for no \(r\), because it would require
  \[
  \frac{100m}{101}\le r<m,
  \]
  but \(\frac{100m}{101}=m-\frac{m}{101}\) lies strictly between \(m-1\) and \(m\).
- For \(1\le n\le 99\), the number of \(r\) such that
  \[
  \left\lfloor \frac{101r}{m}\right\rfloor=n
  \]
  is
  \[
  \left\lfloor \frac{(n+1)m}{101}\right\rfloor-
  \left\lfloor \frac{nm}{101}\right\rfloor.
  \]

Therefore

\[
\sum_{r=1}^{m}2^{-\lfloor 101r/m\rfloor}
=
2^{-101}
+
\sum_{n=1}^{99}
2^{-n}
\left(
\left\lfloor \frac{(n+1)m}{101}\right\rfloor-
\left\lfloor \frac{nm}{101}\right\rfloor
\right).
\]

Summing over \(m=1,\dots,100\),

\[
B=100\cdot 2^{-101}
+
\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}
\sum_{m=1}^{100}
\left(
\left\lfloor \frac{(n+1)m}{101}\right\rfloor-
\left\lfloor \frac{nm}{101}\right\rfloor
\right).
\]

For \(1\le j\le 100\), we use the standard identity

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{100}\left\lfloor \frac{jm}{101}\right\rfloor
=
\frac{100(j-1)}{2}=50(j-1).
\]

Hence for \(1\le n\le 99\),

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{100}
\left(
\left\lfloor \frac{(n+1)m}{101}\right\rfloor-
\left\lfloor \frac{nm}{101}\right\rfloor
\right)
=
50n-50(n-1)=50.
\]

Thus

\[
B=100\cdot 2^{-101}+50\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}.
\]

Now

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{99}2^{-n}=1-2^{-99},
\]

so

\[
B=100\cdot 2^{-101}+50(1-2^{-99})
=50-\frac{100}{2^{101}}.
\]

Finally,

\[
S=\frac{B}{1-2^{-101}}
=
\frac{50-\frac{100}{2^{101}}}{1-\frac{1}{2^{101}}}.
\]

Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(2^{101}\),

\[
S=
\frac{50\cdot 2^{101}-100}{2^{101}-1}
=
\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
